title: digislicer
description: A new SRC machine, DIGISLICER: the SLICE machine with a slice editor. Its SRC page is SLICE's; press SRC again for the editor, where you slice the sample where you want (add at a cursor, split, delete, move, auto-slice on transients, equal grids), watch it play and play slices from the trig keys. A sample's own slices play on every DIGISLICER track and are kept per sample on the +Drive (/cfw/slices.a, .b). With no slices of its own a sample plays AUTO's (slices on the transients). Knob G is STRETCH: the slice's length apart from its pitch (OFF, x0.25 to x3.29), lockable and reachable by the LFOs. PLAY gets PIPO (ping-pong loops). With the keyboard on (FUNC+TRK), the trig keys play the slices, one per key, as the Octatrack's trig slice mode, and live recording records them as slice locks. The stock SLICE machine is left as it is. Its page is drawn by machine-pages (core 3.0), so it combines with the other machines that describe theirs.

summary: FAST AUDIO lowers the DSP load; SYSTEM INFO shows CPU, DSP and memory in the top bar.
title: digihealth
description: Two SETTINGS rows. FAST AUDIO (on by default) runs the audio render's hot code from the free on-chip SRAM: the same code, so the audio is identical and the DSP load lower; a watchdog goes back to the stock code if the copy is ever overwritten. SYSTEM INFO shows CPU, DSP, RAM and free sample memory in the top bar, and a read-only USB diagnostics channel (SysEx device 0x7D) answers tools/digiusb.py.

title: fxkit
description: What the Digitone mk1's effect mods share: one effect at a time has the audio (exclusive, the synths muted), with a mixer around it (the inputs' levels and pans, mix, balance, volume, width), two LFOs with the stock LFO's rates and waves aimed only at its knobs, and p-locks kept in the pattern, in one track's lock table (T4 unless the effect's SETUP says otherwise), that play on their steps and save with the pattern. title: digitables
description: M8-style pitch tables: 16 tables of up to 16 semitone steps, with a length and a loop point, saved with the project. Each note restarts its sound's table and the sequencer's clock steps it. The TBL page (AMP's third page, or TABLES in core-dn1's Mod Menu: hold a track key) has TBL, the table per sound and per trig with p-locks, and SPD, the ticks of 24 PPQN a step, or a fraction of a tick down to a step every audio block (MAX, 1500 a second); hold a track key there for the table editor. A step can ADD a note instead: the note keeps playing and a copy of the trig's note starts at the step's offset, released with it (a strummed chord from one trig). Needs core-dn1 2.2.

title: DigiSwarm
description: An effects engine for the Digitone mk1's audio inputs: eleven engines (SHARDS, SEQ, GLIDE, MIST, DRONE, RAKE, CHOPS, STUTTER, ARP, PATTERN, WARP) with four variations each, a 60-second looper with overdub and undo, Hold, Reverse, a resonant filter, pitch modulation and a reverb with four rooms, in time with the Digitone's tempo, and MIDI CCs for its controls and looper. DIGISWARM in core-dn1's Mod Menu (hold a track key) makes it the active effect and opens its page; while it is active it owns the audio engine (the synths are muted), through fxkit's MIXER (AMP), with two LFOs aimed at its controls (LFO) and p-locks on the pattern's steps (RECORD: hold a trig, turn a control; Hold, Reverse and the engine lock too). MIDI leaves the page to edit the MIDI tracks while it plays; NO turns it off. Needs fxkit (core-dn1 4.1).

A toggles the filter, D cycles six response modes (TILT, DAWN, NOON, DUSK, ECLIPSE, UMBRA), B/C/E/F/G/H edit the amount. summary: A one-shot FM percussion machine for the Digitone mk1/Keys built around the stock FM voice.
on_unit: Tested on hardware; fully functional and stable.
title: DRUM+
description: DRUM+, a percussion machine for the Digitone mk1 that uses the FM kernel as its exciter instead of bypassing it. The machines companion still renders the stock FM voice for a machine's voices, so each hit is built from the FM block the kernel already produced: it is mixed with a pitch-dropping thump, white noise, a short click, a ring modulator, a sample-rate/bit-depth redux and a deep wavefolder. Eight models - KICK, SNARE, HAT, TOM, CLAP, METAL, BONK and ZAP - set the balance, and the borrowed SYN knobs then shape it. Because those knobs are the stock FM parameters' own slots, p-locks, the two system LFOs, MIDI CC and presets work on them, and they keep driving the FM kernel: MODEL is the SYN1 algorithm, TUNE is HARM, DECAY is DTUN, NOISE is FDBK, and the ratio and MIX knobs remain FM's for shaping the exciter. The first SYN1/SYN2 pages are DRUM+'s own: the model is drawn as a 1-pixel drum glyph with its name above it, the parameter bands sit to the right, and the active parameter's value is shown in the centre only while turning. The result runs through the track's filter, mixer, effects and AMP envelope as any machine voice does; the AMP page's stock drive is the saturation stage. Needs core-dn1 4.0 and the machines companion 0.2, on OS 1.44.

summary: A POLY machine: chords from a track's own trigs, borrowing other tracks' voices, and polyphonic MIDI on its channel. Built for machine-pages, which the shop ticks with it.
on_unit: Confirmed on a Digitakt mk1 (OS 1.54), its author reports (2.1); it passes their emulator tests on OS 1.53 and 1.54.
title: Digi Poly
description: Adds a POLY machine (FUNC+SRC list). A POLY track plays chords from its own trigs: its TRIG page becomes the MIDI tracks' one (NOT1-NOT4, VEL, LEN, PROB, LFO.T) with the track's level beside it, and each extra note takes the voice of another track (voice stealing: the voice that started longest ago, never a muted one, one holding a live note or one whose track trigs at the same time). Pressing the track's key plays the whole chord. Notes received on the POLY track's own MIDI channel play polyphonically, one voice per note, and recording them writes the chord into the step's NOT1-NOT4 (up to four notes) instead of a bare trig. On its TRIG page the LEVEL knob sets the track level and the LEV fader shows it, as on the audio pages. SETTINGS > POLY chooses which tracks lend their voice to the pool; that is kept in the kit, so each pattern has its own voice allocation and it is saved with the project. A stolen voice plays the POLY track's sound, follows its knobs and level while it does, and gets its own sound back at its next trig. Kits saved with POLY load as ONESHOT on the stock OS. POLY is machine 6. 2.1: its page is drawn by elekloader's machine-pages mod (core 3.0 or later), which elekloader ticks with it.

on_unit: Confirmed on a Digitakt mk1, its author reports; it passes their emulator tests on OS 1.53 and 1.54.
title: Digi Matrix
description: A modulation matrix: any track's LFO can modulate any parameter of any track. SETTINGS > MOD MATRIX opens a page with 8 routing slots; each one picks a source (a track and one of its two LFOs), a destination (a track and one of its sound parameters), its own depth (-64..+64, independent of the source LFO's own DEP) and whether that LFO still modulates its own track as well. UP/DOWN choose a slot, YES turns it on and off, NO leaves, and the knobs edit the slot under the cursor: A source track, B source LFO, C destination track, D destination parameter, E depth, F own track on/off. The matrix is kept in the kit (two unused parameter slots of each track's sound), so every pattern has its own and it is saved with the project.

Master ring modulator, a low-shelf/high-shelf master EQ (TILT), a Crunch/Redux lo-fi stage (BITS / SR / CRUNCH), a wavefolder with a continuous CLEAN/MUD/DIST/TRSH fold type, a five-mode modulation insert (PITCH: WOB / SHFT, STEREO: FLAN / PAN / WIDE), an output meter and a soft output ceiling. Seven pages after the stock master pages (FUNC+LFO; LEFT/RIGHT rotate the pages): DIGI RING, FOLD, TILT, CRUSH, PITCH, STEREO and PERFORM. title: Compressor gain-reduction preview
description: One more compressor page holding a scrolling trace of estimated gain reduction, reached by pressing the compressor page key again, which then returns to the stock page. FUNC + the page key switches its layout: the level, threshold and GR together, or GR alone with 0 dB at the top. It is stock page 11 listed twice in the view's page vector rather than a new page id, so stock's parameter lookup, title and encoder mapping are inherited unchanged and the entries are told apart by the view's selected index in the draw slot. The estimate builds each side of the compressor's input from the audio interrupt's receive buffer - the eight voice slots split by pan, dropped when off the main bus, slots 5 and 6 trimmed, plus the PRE delay and reverb returns - through the master distortion and its symmetry and each SEQ's sidechain, into a 5 ms peak detector on the louder side. A static curve that THR slides along the level axis gives the demand, and one attack/release pole a block follows it. The model and every calibrated value: re/subsystems/compressor-model.md. Hardware-verified 2026-09-20: the page, hook, renderer, scroll and producer all run, and an on-device null of the input model against the MAIN pair reads near zero. Accuracy and known limits: re/subsystems/compressor-model.md. The main ones: on random settings over drum patterns it was not fitted on, the estimate reads 1.6 dB rms from the measured reduction with no bias (2026-09-26), a steady tone 0.56; DIST symmetry away from 64 is outside the model; the reduction past 36 dB is capped; POST returns are not modelled and PRE returns join the sum about 4 ms early; and material whose crest factor is far from the calibration tone's reads off. Port of rytm-mods 0006-comp-preview. From 1.1 the preview is listed in the COMP view through core-ar2 0.4's page lists, so other mods' pages can sit beside it (needs core 0.4, OS 1.74 only).

description: NO + PLAY becomes an A/B between the kit as edited and as saved. The first press keeps the edits in a stash and reloads the saved kit, under stock's popup ("KIT 1 RELOADED!"); the next puts the edits back ("EDITS RESTORED!"). Editing while the original plays ends the A/B: the next press keeps those edits instead, dropping the stashed ones, and reloads as a first press does. The same happens after a change of kit or any other reload, found by a checksum of the working kit taken after each press. A press on a kit with no edits is a plain reload and arms nothing. Repoints both single-kit reload calls and their popups' text: the key handler's NO + PLAY (0x400cd4ae, "KIT %d RELOADED!") and kit_reload_key (0x400dd5de, "KIT RELOADED!"). The stash, one 0x9e3-byte kit, comes from the firmware's heap on the first press. The restore copies it back and applies it exactly as stock's reload applies the saved kit, including kit_mark(working, 0), whose meaning is not established. Reloading every kit stays stock. Port of rytm-mods 0010-kit-ab.

title: Main output level light
description: On both compressor pages - stock's and 0006's preview - the VOL knob's label draws inverted while the main output's RMS level is over rms_db, for gain staging. The level is the louder of MAIN L and R, each a mean square averaged with a 300 ms time constant; a full-scale square wave reads 0 dBFS and a full-scale sine -3.01. The label turns on above the threshold and off 1 dB below it. MAIN is read each audio interrupt from the receive buffer - the pair USB and the sampler record, after the compressor. The master volume knob does not set that pair, though an interaction in the circuit moves it by up to a few dB over the knob's travel. The label is inverted by XOR in the box stock highlights labels with, so a label stock has already highlighted reads normal while over. The drawing reaches the compressor view only: its vtable's two knob draw slots point at wrappers, which run stock's draw and then the inversion. Began as a clip indicator (any MAIN sample at -0.07 dBFS). Measured 2026-09-26, the Rytm's USB MAIN showed no saturation at any compressor VOL - no pile-up at the ceiling, no flattened peaks, no added harmonics - and the audible distortion was the monitoring interface's input, so a level reference for gain staging replaced it. title: DAC sum, voice filter, shaper and polarity
description: All eight voices leave the analog main bus and reach it again through the DAC, panned and summed on the ColdFire: the groundwork for processing a voice after its analog filter, such as a digital filter. The route mask store in the audio interrupt sets every voice's main-disable bit. After the receive buffer fills, each voice slot - the voice after its analog filter and amp, before pan - is split by the pan of its VCA words, as 0006 does, and the two sums are added to the PRE return pair of the output ring, which enters the analog mix ahead of the master distortion and compressor. A voice whose track stock has off the main bus stays out of the sum. The cost is fixed per block; nothing stands aside. Each voice is filtered first, set on a second FILTER page, DAC FILTER, reached by pressing FILTER again while DAC SUM is on. Its top row is FRQ, RES, TYP and DEP; stock's FILTER graph is drawn over FRQ and RES from FRQ, TYP and (for the 2-pole types) RES, a flat line when TYP is OFF. TYP runs in stock's FILTER order - OFF, LP2, LP1, BP, HP1, HP2, BS, PK - and shows stock's TYP glyph and popup, or OFF. LP1 and HP1 are a bilinear first-order section (6 dB/oct, exactly -3 dB at the cutoff); the others a biquad each (the RBJ cookbook's sections, BP with 0 dB at the centre, BS the notch). FRQ is stock's FRQ scale, a semitone a step with 440 Hz at 60, and its popup is stock's FRQ popup, so it reads in hertz where 0008 is built. RES sets the 2-pole types' Q, exponentially from RES 0: 0.707 to 2.0 for LP2 and HP2 (a peak up to +6.3 dB), 0.5 to 8 for BP, BS and PK (width only); LP1 and HP1 have none. DEP mixes the filtered voice with the dry one: 0 dB, then 0.25 dB steps of cut to -31.5 dB, then FULL, the plain filter. Below FULL, HP1 and HP2 give low shelves, LP1 and LP2 high shelves, BP cuts all but the band and BS is a bell cut of DEP's depth, the poles staying at FRQ. For PK, DEP is a boost instead, +0.0 to +6.0 dB over its range, built on BP. A slot's coefficients are worked out again only when its values change; switching between LP1 and HP1 at one FRQ carries the filter's state over (LP1 = x - HP1), so it should not click, but other type switches can. The TYP and RES knobs take stock TYP's and RES's encoder range and acceleration, copied into their records each idle tick, and TYP keeps its fractional delta, so both step as stock's. The 2-pole types run after the 1-pole pass, each slot on one of them through its biquad in place (direct form I, five multiplies a frame); a slot on none costs a few instructions a block, so the cost follows the voices using them. The coefficients are Q30, worked out in the interrupt when the slot's entry changes, from cos and sin of w0 per FRQ step (cave16), 1/a0 by divu.l and one Newton step; modelled against floating point over every type and FRQ, none is unstable and each lies within 3e-5 of its float design. The EMAC's << scale factor is not used: the first 2-pole build relied on it and BP came out silent and the other types wrong, as a model with the scale ignored predicts; Q30 products are now doubled after movclr, and the filter sums its terms at half scale and doubles with saturation. The DAC FILTER page's bottom row holds a transient shaper's ATK and SUS and POL. ATK and SUS run -64..+63, 0 the centre, drawn as SAMPLE FINE's dial (dotted at 0) and stepped as stock's PAN; FUNC + turn snaps to the next of -64, 0 and +63 once the turn adds up to `snap` steps one way. Full scale is 12 dB of attack or sustain change on a strong transient, the total boost capped at +6 dB. POL (+ or -) inverts the voice's contribution to the sum, folded into its pan gains, so it costs nothing; the individual outputs are untouched. The shaper runs after the filters and before the sum, a slot at a time for each voice whose track has ATK or SUS set. Once a block it takes the slot's peak and moves three followers - instant attack with 40 ms release, 15 ms attack with 150 ms release, instant attack with 300 ms release - and from dB(fast / slow) (the attack) and dB(hold / fast) (the sustain), each clipped to 12 dB, works out a gain, 0 dB below -60 dBFS. A block's own peak sets its gain (two passes: the peak, then the scaling), ramped from the last block's across it, or stepping there when it moves more than 3 dB, as at an onset. Levels in dB come from a normalisation and a 128-entry table, the gain from a 0.25 dB table, applied at half scale and doubled with saturation. A voice turned on starts its followers at its first block's peak. With ATK and SUS 0 on every voice track the shaper is skipped outright, a test a block (a flag the idle tick sets, so turning one on takes up to a tick); a voice at 0 among others is skipped and untouched. It was modelled in tools/voice_dac_shaper.py on captured voices first, and the device's integer code emulated against that model within 0.1 dB. Its knobs reuse ids 7 and 14 (Error records) and 457 (CB TEST's CB_OSC_SELECT, a hidden machine's, which stock never shows), renamed. From 1.2 the values are kept in core-ar2 0.3's mod storage, per sound as before: two sound fields, vd_flt (24 bits: TYP << 21 | (FRQ ^ 0x7f) << 14 | (DEP ^ 0x7f) << 7 | RES) and vd_shp (15 bits: ATK << 8 | SUS << 1 | POL, ATK and SUS 7-bit two's complement), read and written with core_store_get and core_store_set on the live sound, so zero is TYP OFF, FRQ 127, DEP FULL, RES 0, ATK and SUS 0, POL +. Core keeps them in the live sound's spare bytes and the velocity routes' amount low bytes, saves and loads them with the sound and clears them in sound_init_defaults, so they travel with the sound - kit save and reload, pattern kit changes, the sound pool, copy and paste - and a sound reset resets DAC FILTER with the rest. Core also owns the sound push and the VELOCITY MOD menu's amount hooks; voice-dac no longer touches stored records or the route bytes itself. A tick in the UI's idle routine copies each track's values into the tables the audio interrupt reads, which never calls core; an edit updates its track's entry at once, and core's ev_project clears the tables after a project load until the next tick. Each change ends with the notice stock's sound settings setters send, SoundConfigChangedInfo through the track's sound accessor; without it a change played and survived a kit save but was lost at a reboot without one. Settings saved by voice-dac 1.0/1.1 or rytm-mods 0013 (stored slots 42..47, globals +12/+13) load as the defaults. The hardware notes below are for 1.1, whose storage this replaced. Hardware, 2026-10-07, POL in slot 43: POL - survives a reboot without a kit save, a kit save and reboot, the sound pool onto another track and NO + PLAY; a sound saved by the build before loads POL +. Before this, the save kept only TYP's bits of +0x6d and POL was lost at a reload or a reboot. Hardware, 2026-10-06, the shaper build: ATK and SUS shape onsets and tails as in the prototype, POL inverts, nothing is heard with both 0, values survive a reboot with and without a kit save, FUNC snaps, and the dial draws dotted at 0. Kits saved while the route-byte probe ran read ATK and SUS +63 (their marker, 90, clamped). Hardware, 2026-10-06, the 2-pole build: each type sounds as its glyph across FRQ; RES peaks LP2 and HP2 and narrows BP, BS and PK; DEP below FULL gives the shelves and BS's bell cut, PK's boost reading +0.0 to +6.0 dB; the bottom of the FRQ range is clean; TYP and RES survive a reboot with and without a kit save; TYP and RES step as stock's. Kits saved while the route-byte probe ran carry its marker, 0x5a, in every route byte: RES reads 90 on them. Hardware, 2026-10-06, dbg build: kits saved with the tagged bytes load the same values; untouched, stock-saved and reset sounds read the defaults; values survive a reboot with and without a kit save, the sound pool, copy/paste, NO + PLAY and a pattern change to another kit; the previous build reads kits this one saved. The route bytes' markers survive a kit save and reboot, amount edits, FUNC reset, destination changes and CLEAR/PASTE MODULATIONS and their UNDO in both menus, and no engine route word carried one. Hardware, 2026-09-29, DAC FILTER: TYP and DEP survive a reboot without a kit save (with the notice; not without it) and a kit save and reboot. An untouched sound reads DEP FULL (it read 0 dB while the default's DEP field was lost to a `|` the assembler takes as a comment). The screen is right: the popups (FRQ in hertz, DEP in dB and FULL, TYP), TYP's glyph and OFF, and the graph in the top row, flat in OFF. The rest of the HIGH-PASS list below: each mode sounds right across FRQ and DEP; the sound pool, copy/paste, NO + PLAY kit reload and a pattern change to another kit and back are not yet checked for this version. DAC SUM, the last item of AUDIO ROUTING, switches it at run time. OFF is stock's routing and no sum. It is kept with the project's globals, in core-ar2's global field vd_dac, one bit per global slot (index = the slot, from the active live record's address: 0x413192ff + 228 x slot). Each slot keeps its own value; the UI's idle tick and core's ev_project follow the active one. A slot saved without it loads as OFF, and a global slot received as SysEx loads it OFF (core keeps no mod data for those). 1.1 kept it in stored bytes +12/+13, which are stock's TRACK 1 and TRACK 2 MIDI CHANNEL: 1.2 no longer overwrites them. The item is built after USB TO MAIN with USB OUT's sequence and managers; its value draws as ON or OFF and changes with the value controls, up for ON. Switching clicks once: the analog bus changes at once, the DAC path 2.58 ms later. Hardware, 2026-09-28, the HIGH-PASS version this page replaced (one knob, HPF), with the shipping mods: the page shows only while DAC SUM is on, the knob and its popup work, each track keeps its own value, and 0004's LFO RND and 0008's FRQ popup are unaffected. The value survives kit save and reload, another kit loaded and back, a pattern change to another kit and back, NO + PLAY kit reload, the sound pool, sound copy/paste and a power cycle - with a kit save before it, as that version wrote the sound without the change notice; an untouched sound reads OFF. Muted tracks go silent with DAC SUM on as with it off. DAC SUM survives power cycles, on and off, without a project save. CPU, 2026-10-06, the burn build (tools/voice_dac_burn.py) with 0006's telemetry, in the worst case: A16 playing, DAC SUM on, every voice track LP1, the compressor preview page up. With nothing added 0013 took 4.24% of a block, the UI event queue held at about 2, BgWorker had jobs pending in every frame and 0006's estimator stood aside in every frame. Added interrupt time did not make the queue run away: each step raised it to a new level it then held for the minute - about 20 at +0.5%, 59 at +1%, 104 at +1.5%, 147 at +2% - so the UI kept up but further behind, and the preview page's scrolling visibly paused from +0.5%. An earlier 10 s sweep without a drain between steps read that climb as a runaway; at +8% the device's USB audio dropped and it needed a reboot. Where the UI stops answering lies above +2%, not measured. New per-voice stages cost in proportion to the voices using them, as each is skipped when off; this worst case is not the one to size them against. Headroom, 2026-09-28, the timing build's peak and clip counters over A01-A16 and B01-B05 with DAC SUM on and every HPF off (build/mix/20260928_145359, tools/voice_dac_headroom.py): the DAC sum, PRE returns included, peaked at -12.3 dBFS at most (A16; -21.6 at least, A09), and no side-frame reached full scale on any pattern. The filter skips a pair of slots that are both off (TYP OFF or DEP 0 dB), keeping its state on the signal so turning a filter on does not click (by ear, 2026-09-28, HIGH-PASS version). From the profile, that took the stub from about 3.2% of a block to about 1.6% with no HPF engaged, about 0.4% a pair engaged. The DAC FILTER version, timing build, 2026-09-29, one session, all eight voices playing: 2.44% of a block (median; 2.87% p99) with every TYP OFF, 3.96% (4.26% p99, 4.48% max) with every voice track LP1 - 0.38% a pair, as the HIGH-PASS filter's. Coefficients are worked out only when a slot's values change, so the steady state adds a compare a slot. The route byte's only other writers are analog circuit calibration's, which only ever take voices off the bus (compressor-hardware.md), so nothing puts the analog path back under the DAC path. Hardware, 2026-09-28, before the switch: the voices sounded right, the pan split matched stock within 0.01 per slot over USB, the latency was 2.58 ms and the polarity was inverted, since fixed. K and the slot trims were then set from A/Bs on and off: slots 0-3 and 5 match the analog path within 0.1 dB; slot 6's trim was corrected from the same measurement and not measured again. Known limits: the voices reach MAIN 2.58 ms later than they would through the analog bus. They share the PRE pair with the delay and reverb returns and the PRE-FX audio input, and are clamped at its full scale (about 12 dB above the loudest pattern measured). Individual outputs are unaffected, and carry the voice before the filter. TYP, FRQ and DEP cannot be p-locked or reached over MIDI: they live outside the sound's 42 parameters. Switching TYP between LP1 and HP1 clicks on a sound with much energy at either end (hardware, 2026-09-29): the state carries over, but the output changes from one filter's to the other's at once; a crossfade would take it away. The graph draws LP1's slope right of the FRQ point and HP1's left of it, as stock's FILTER graph does. The slot 4 and 7 trims rest on one pattern each. With DAC SUM on the USB voice channels carry the filtered voices. Port of rytm-mods 0013-voice-dac. From 1.3 the page goes through core-ar2 0.4's page tables and page-key lists (needs core 0.4, OS 1.74 only). From 1.4 (rytm-mods 3a98e23) the page's knobs follow TYP: with LP1 or HP1 RES's slot is empty, and with TYP OFF FRQ's and RES's too - no dial or label, and the knob does nothing, as on stock's REVERB and DISTORTION pages - and the graph clears stock's empty-knob marks under it; the entry comes from core-ar2 0.6's core_page_fns (needs core 0.6).
